title: CVE-2026-3864: CSI Driver for NFS path traversal via subDir may delete unintended directories on the NFS server

qa_pairs.question: For CVE-2026-3864 in Kubernetes' CSI Driver for NFS (`nfs.csi.k8s.io`), a path traversal issue was reported where the `subDir` parameter in volume identifiers is insufficiently validated. An attacker who can create PersistentVolumes referencing the NFS CSI driver could craft volume identifiers containing `../`, and during volume deletion or cleanup the driver could operate on unintended directories outside the intended managed path within the NFS export, potentially deleting or modifying directories on the NFS server. The CVSS vector is `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H` with Medium severity 6.5. How do I know whether my cluster is vulnerable, how should I mitigate it, what version contains the fix, and how can I detect possible exploitation?
qa_pairs.answer: You may be vulnerable if you run the CSI Driver for NFS, allow users to create PersistentVolumes referencing it, and are on a driver version that does not validate traversal sequences in the `subDir` field. All CSI Driver for NFS versions before v4.13.1 are affected; versions >= v4.13.1 are fixed. Mitigations are to upgrade to a patched version, restrict PersistentVolume creation privileges to trusted administrators, and ensure NFS exports only allow the driver to write intended directories. For detection, inspect NFS CSI PersistentVolumes' `volumeHandle` for traversal such as `../` and review CSI controller logs for unexpected directory operations such as `Removing subPath: /tmp/mount-uuid/legitimate/../../../exports/subdir`.

title: client-go/gentype: fake.go in production package disables Go linker dead code elimination (+52 MB binary bloat)

qa_pairs.question:
In Kubernetes/client-go, is the following binary bloat issue in `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` something the Kubernetes project should fix, for example by moving `fake.go` out of the production package or putting it behind a build tag?

## Summary

The `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` package includes `fake.go` in the same Go package as production code (`type.go`). Because Go compiles all non-test `.go` files in a package together, `fake.go`'s import of `k8s.io/client-go/testing` is included in every binary that uses typed Kubernetes clients — even when no fake/test code is used.

This transitively pulls in `google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/descfmt` and `google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl`, which use `reflect.MethodByName` with non-constant arguments. When the Go linker detects `reflect.MethodByName` is reachable, it conservatively disables dead code elimination for all exported methods on all reachable types. This causes massive binary bloat for any program that also imports packages with large method sets, like `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2`.

## Impact

Adding a blank import of `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` to a program that uses the AWS EC2 SDK increases binary size by +52 MB, from 13 MB to 65 MB, linking 2,273 `ec2.Client` methods instead of the 7 actually needed.

This affects every consumer of typed Kubernetes clients (`kubernetes/typed/*/v*`), since they all import `gentype`.

## Root Cause

The import chain:

```text
k8s.io/client-go/gentype (fake.go)
  └─ k8s.io/client-go/testing
       ├─ k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields
       └─ k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch
            └─ ... (several hops) ...
                 └─ google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/descfmt
                      └─ reflect.ValueOf(vs).MethodByName("Get")  [stringer.go:44, 99]
                 └─ google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/impl
                      └─ reflect.PtrTo(t).MethodByName(...)  [message.go:198, 201]
```

The Go linker sees `reflect.MethodByName` is reachable and disables method pruning globally. See golang/go#25081 and kubernetes/kubernetes#132216 for background.

## Reproduction

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $DIR" EXIT
cd "$DIR"

go mod init gentype-dce-repro

cat > baseline.go << 'GOEOF'
//go:build baseline
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2"
)

type EC2API interface {
    DescribeInstances(ctx context.Context, params *ec2.DescribeInstancesInput, optFns ...func(*ec2.Options)) (*ec2.DescribeInstancesOutput, error)
}

func main() {
    cfg, _ := config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.Background())
    var client EC2API = ec2.NewFromConfig(cfg)
    out, _ := client.DescribeInstances(context.Background(), &ec2.DescribeInstancesInput{InstanceIds: []string{"i-test"}})
    fmt.Println(out)
}
GOEOF

cat > with_gentype.go << 'GOEOF'
//go:build with_gentype
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/config"
    "github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/ec2"
    _ "k8s.io/client-go/gentype"
)

type EC2API interface {
    DescribeInstances(ctx context.Context, params *ec2.DescribeInstancesInput, optFns ...func(*ec2.Options)) (*ec2.DescribeInstancesOutput, error)
}

func main() {
    cfg, _ := config.LoadDefaultConfig(context.Background())
    var client EC2API = ec2.NewFromConfig(cfg)
    out, _ := client.DescribeInstances(context.Background(), &ec2.DescribeInstancesInput{InstanceIds: []string{"i-test"}})
    fmt.Println(out)
}
GOEOF

go mod tidy

echo "=== Go version ==="
go version

echo ""
echo "=== Baseline (EC2 SDK only) ==="
go build -tags baseline -o bin_baseline .
echo "Size: $(stat --format=%s bin_baseline) bytes ($(du -h bin_baseline | cut -f1))"
echo "ec2.Client methods linked: $(go tool nm bin_baseline | grep -c 'service/ec2\.(\*Client)\.')"

echo ""
echo "=== With gentype (blank import) ==="
go build -tags with_gentype -o bin_gentype .
echo "Size: $(stat --format=%s bin_gentype) bytes ($(du -h bin_gentype | cut -f1))"
echo "ec2.Client methods linked: $(go tool nm bin_gentype | grep -c 'service/ec2\.(\*Client)\.')"
```

### Results

Using Go 1.26.1 linux/amd64, client-go v0.35.2, and ec2 v1.294.1:

| Build | Binary Size | `ec2.Client` methods linked |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (EC2 SDK only) | 13 MB | 7 (just `DescribeInstances` + helpers) |
| + `k8s.io/client-go/gentype` (blank import) | 65 MB | 2,273 (all EC2 API operations) |
| Difference | +52 MB | +2,266 dead methods |

## Suggested Fix

Move `fake.go` out of the `gentype` package so that test fake infrastructure is not compiled into production binaries. Options:

1. Move to a subpackage: `k8s.io/client-go/gentype/fake`, analogous to how `k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake` is separate from `k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes`.
2. Use a build tag: add a build constraint to `fake.go` to exclude it from production builds.

Either approach would break the `gentype -> testing -> protobuf -> reflect.MethodByName` chain for production builds, allowing the Go linker to properly eliminate dead code.

Additional investigation suggested a Go 1.26-specific regression in `google.golang.org/protobuf`: Go 1.26 added `reflect.Value.Methods()`, and protobuf's `internal/descfmt/stringer.go` calls `MethodByName("Methods")`, causing the linker to retain `reflect.Value.Methods()` and disable dead code elimination globally for all exported methods on all reachable types. This can affect any Go 1.26 binary that transitively imports `google.golang.org/protobuf`, including paths through `k8s.io/client-go/discovery`, `github.com/prometheus/client_golang`, or other protobuf consumers. The protobuf fixes were merged upstream but not yet released at the time of the report.
qa_pairs.answer: The issue was closed as not actionable for Kubernetes. The investigation found that Kubernetes had already addressed the protobuf regression in #137451 by pinning protobuf to a commit with the Go 1.26 DCE fix for Kubernetes server binaries. For Cobra-based projects, dead code elimination is disabled regardless of protobuf because Cobra imports `text/template`, whose `exec.go` uses `reflect.Value.MethodByName(fieldName)` with a runtime-variable argument; the root cause is tracked in Go issue golang/go#25081. Moving `fake.go` to a subpackage would be good hygiene, but was not expected to produce measurable binary-size improvements for real-world consumers because other import paths already trigger the same linker behavior.

title: CVE-2026-3288: ingress-nginx rewrite-target nginx configuration injection

qa_pairs.question: For CVE-2026-3288, ingress-nginx rewrite-target nginx configuration injection, the issue lists CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H. If I understand correctly, to exploit this vulnerability an attacker must be authenticated to the Kubernetes cluster and have a role with permissions to modify Ingress objects. Is that correct? If so, should the CVSS Attack Vector (AV) be Local and Privileges Required (PR) be High instead of AV:N and PR:L?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, the vulnerability scope/impact is correctly understood as a privilege escalation from a user with permission to create an Ingress to probably cluster admin, depending on cluster configuration. The maintainer explained that Kubernetes CVEs rarely use CVSS Local because Local means access to the server where the Kubernetes component runs, such as a control plane node. Privileges Required is evaluated from the cluster operator perspective: in this case, Low corresponds to engineers/users who can run workloads but do not administer the cluster, while High would mean cluster administrators themselves. For more context, they pointed to the Kubernetes Security Response Committee severity-ratings documentation (https://github.com/kubernetes/committee-security-response/blob/main/severity-ratings.md).

title: PaymentServicesPaypal module implicitly depends on InventoryInStorePickupFrontend module and breaks the checkout

qa_pairs.question: In Magento 2.4.7-p8 with Payment Services module version 2.13.0, with `Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend` disabled along with other `Magento_Inventory*` modules, checkout breaks on the payment step. Steps: 1. Add product to cart 2. Go to checkout 3. Fill in shipping information and go to Payment step 4. Review Shipping Information in the Order Summary block. Expected: Shipping Information is visible and displays the actual shipping data as it did on Payment Services module version 2.11.0. Actual: Shipping Information is empty and there is a JavaScript error in the console. The suspected cause is that `vendor/magento/module-inventory-in-store-pickup-frontend/view/frontend/web/js/view/shipping-information-ext.js` declares `isStorePickup`, but because `Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend` is disabled, that mixin is not loaded. `Magento_PaymentServicesPaypal` adds `vendor/magento/module-payment-services-paypal/view/frontend/web/js/view/shipping-information-mixin.js` and overwrites the original `shipping-information.html` template, where it calls `<!-- ko if: (!isStorePickup()) -->`, but the function is not found. Does `Magento_PaymentServicesPaypal` implicitly depend on `Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend`, and what version or change fixes the broken checkout shipping information?
qa_pairs.answer: The issue is present in `magento/module-payment-services-paypal` v2.13.0 but not in v2.14.0; it was fixed somewhere between those versions. In `vendor/magento/module-payment-services-paypal/view/frontend/web/template/shipping-information.html`, v2.13.0 used `<!-- ko if: (!isStorePickup()) -->`, while v2.14.0 uses `<!-- ko if: (typeof isStorePickup !== 'function' || !isStorePickup()) -->`.

title: SRI hashes stop checkout from loading static.js and mixins.js when bundling and minify is enabled

qa_pairs.question:
In Magento 2.4.8-p3 with the CSP module enabled, production mode, and JavaScript bundling and minification enabled, checkout stops loading `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js`. Steps to reproduce:

1. Set store to production mode
2. Enable bundling and minify options for JS
3. Deploy the content
4. Add item to cart and browse to checkout
5. Check to see if static.min.js and mixins.min.js were loaded onto the page

Expected result: the JS files are added to the `<head>` section and loaded on the page.

Actual result: both files are missing from the page.

It looks related to recent changes in `Magento/Csp/Model/Deploy/Package/Processor/PostProcessor/Integrity.php` that write all integrity hashes during deployment, plus the new `GenerateBundleAssetIntegrity.php`. The hashes are written using the non-minified filenames `static.js` and `mixins.js` instead of the deployed `.min.js` filenames. Previously, `sri-hashes.json` only contained hashes for `requirejs-config.min.js`, so bundle files stayed in the same group and the Config block could add JS files correctly. Now the bundle hashes are correctly found with `.min.js` names and put in separate asset groups, but hashes for `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js` are looked up as `static.js` and `mixins.js`, so Magento tries to insert them into an existing JS asset group where the bundle files are not present and fails to add them. The only workaround found is disabling JS minification or bundling.

Is there a patch or fix for this SRI/bundling/minification issue?
qa_pairs.answer: A patch was created for this issue at https://gist.github.com/hryvinskyi/3df14e684d67bd8f7d278f4340ab133b. The maintainer stated that the patch fixes the missing `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js` issue when bundling and minification are enabled, and also fixes corrupted `sri-hashes.json` files caused by concurrent write race conditions.

title: Magento\SalesRule\Model\Plugin\QuoteConfigProductAttributes::afterGetProductAttributes getting triggered on all Cart Queries

qa_pairs.question:
In Magento, on all versions, `Magento\SalesRule\Model\Plugin\QuoteConfigProductAttributes::afterGetProductAttributes` appears to trigger `salesrule_product_attributes` table selects and retrieve sales rule attribute data from EAV even when `collectTotals` has not fired.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Add products to cart; `collectTotals` should have completed here.
2. Enable DB Query Log.
3. Hit the cart page URL.
4. To confirm the query fired, run `cat var/log/db.log | grep "salesrule_product_attribute"` from the Magento root.

Expected result: the `salesrule_product_attribute` query should be fired only when `collectTotals` is happening.

Actual result: the `salesrule_product_attribute` query is fired always.

For large catalogs and companies running many promotions, this matters. If there is no need for `collectTotals` to run, which is a heavy process, why should this plugin run and retrieve data? On a million-product catalog, this table can contain a few 100k rows, which adds load time and leads to a performance bottleneck. Is this expected behavior, or should it be addressed?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer confirmed this as a performance issue after deeper analysis. The plugin fires on every quote item collection load, not just during totals collection, causing unnecessary `salesrule_product_attribute` queries and EAV attribute loading even when totals are not recalculated. Suggested potential solutions were lazy loading only when `collectTotals()` runs, adding a conditional flag before loading attributes, caching active attributes per store/customer group, or moving the loading closer to rule validation during totals collection.

title: Public accessibility of cron.php causes errors and security concerns

qa_pairs.question:
In Magento / Adobe Commerce 2.4.8, after installing Magento 2, I can open a browser and navigate to `https://yourdomain.com/cron.php`. I expected `cron.php` not to be publicly accessible in a production environment, and expected Magento cron jobs to run only via CLI (`bin/magento cron:run`) and system cron tasks. Instead, `cron.php` appears to be exposed to the web by default, and if executed via HTTP it can cause runtime errors such as:

`TypeError: implode(): Argument #1 ($array) must be of type array, string given in /app/bvu7cj4frt2um/vendor/magento/module-cron/Observer/ProcessCronQueueObserver.php:967`

This exposure looks like a legacy carryover from Magento 1 web crons on shared hosting. Current Adobe Commerce documentation recommends system-level CLI cron only (`bin/magento cron:run`). In modern deployments, `cron.php` does not seem required, but its presence in `pub/` causes confusion about best practices and may unnecessarily increase the attack surface. Should `cron.php` be publicly accessible / officially supported, or should it be blocked or considered deprecated?
qa_pairs.answer:
The response was that `pub/.htaccess` should contain rules that prevent execution of `cron.php`, and the linked Magento `pub/.htaccess` lines were pointed to as the relevant configuration. For NGINX, the equivalent `.htaccess` rules should be converted into NGINX configuration. Later verification on the `2.4-develop` branch found the issue not reproducible on both Apache and NGINX because both returned a 404, and a maintainer agreed that the web version of `cron.php` is not recommended and confirmed the issue for contribution.

https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/c8ff03033f9d79d9e6b6482086940153a28c6443/pub/.htaccess#L225-L234

```
## Deny access  to cron.php
    <Files cron.php>
        <IfVersion < 2.4>
            order allow,deny
            deny from all
        </IfVersion>
        <IfVersion >= 2.4>
            Require all denied
        </IfVersion>
    </Files>
```

In Magento 2.4.8-p2, calling `InvoiceService::prepareInvoice($order)` appears to mutate the same `$order` object's entity type from `order` to `invoice`. Is this a confirmed Magento issue, and if so where/when is it fixed?

Reproduction:
```php
/** @var \Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository */
/** @var \Magento\Sales\Model\Service\InvoiceService $invoiceService */

$orderId = 7030365; // use a valid order_id that can be invoiced
```

title: Error. Could not save child: "Unknown entity type: Magento\Bundle\Model\Selection\Interceptor requested"

qa_pairs.answer: The issue was reproduced on the `2.4-develop` branch and confirmed. `Magento\Bundle\Model\Selection` uses the EntityManager rather than `AbstractDb`, and it is registered in the MetadataPool in `app/code/Magento/Bundle/etc/di.xml`; when a plugin is applied, Magento generates `Magento\Bundle\Model\Selection\Interceptor`, and `EntityManager::save()` calls `TypeResolver::resolve()` with that interceptor class. Because TypeResolver has no explicit mapping for interceptors of concrete classes, the MetadataPool lookup fails with the unknown entity type exception. The recommended approach is to avoid plugging into `Magento\Bundle\Model\Selection` directly and instead target `Magento\Bundle\Model\ResourceModel\Selection` or use the appropriate API/data interfaces.

title: `check_header_validity` does not reject null bytes and ASCII control characters in header names and values

qa_pairs.question:
In psf/requests, `check_header_validity` in `requests/utils.py` appears to silently accept null bytes (`\x00`) and other ASCII control characters (`\x01`–`\x1f`, `\x7f`) in both header names and values. RFC 7230 Section 3.2.6 forbids these characters in header fields, but only `\r` and `\n` seem to be caught.

Expected result: `check_header_validity` should raise `InvalidHeader` for any header name or value containing null bytes or ASCII control characters, consistent with how `\r` and `\n` are already handled.

Actual result:
```python
from requests.utils import check_header_validity
check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'val\x00ue'))   # no error raised
check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'val\x01ue'))   # no error raised
check_header_validity(('X-Test\x00', 'value'))   # no error raised
```

Reproduction:
```python
from requests.utils import check_header_validity
from requests.exceptions import InvalidHeader

# All of these should raise InvalidHeader but do not:
check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'val\x00ue'))
check_header_validity(('X-Test', '\x01value'))
check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'value\x7f'))
check_header_validity(('X-Test\x00', 'value'))

# These correctly raise InvalidHeader:
# check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'val\nue'))   # blocked
# check_header_validity(('X-Test', 'val\rue'))   # blocked
```

Should Requests reject `\x00` and other ASCII control characters in header names and values, and what change is needed?
qa_pairs.answer:
RFC 7230 Section 3.2.6 defines valid header field characters as VCHAR (visible ASCII, `\x21`-`\x7e`) plus obs-text. Null bytes (`\x00`) and ASCII control characters (`\x01`-`\x1f`, `\x7f`) are explicitly forbidden in both header names and values — they can lead to header injection attacks or silent truncation by intermediate proxies.

The current regex in `requests/utils.py` only catches `\r` and `\n`:
```python
# Current (incomplete)
_CLEAN_HEADER_REGEX_BYTE = re.compile(b"^\S[^\r\n]*$|^$")
_CLEAN_HEADER_REGEX_STR  = re.compile(r"^\S[^\r\n]*$|^$")
```

The fix is to extend the rejected character set to cover all ASCII control chars and NUL:
```python
# Fixed — rejects \x00-\x1f and \x7f
_CLEAN_HEADER_REGEX_BYTE = re.compile(b"^[\x20-\x7e\x80-\xff]*$|^$")
_CLEAN_HEADER_REGEX_STR  = re.compile(r"^[\x20-\x7e\x80-\xff]*$|^$")
```

Or equivalently using a negative character class:
```python
_CLEAN_HEADER_REGEX_STR = re.compile(r"^[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$")
```

Header names additionally must not contain separators (`()<>@,;:\"/[]?={} \t`), but fixing the control character gap is the higher-priority security issue.

This is also worth checking against `urllib3`'s `_validate_header_parts()` since requests delegates actual socket writes there — a defense-in-depth fix in requests is still worthwhile so it fails before the network layer.

title: TooManyRedirects exception loop when requesting FQDN URLs with a trailing dot

qa_pairs.question:
In psf/requests, making a request to a URL with a fully qualified domain name that includes a trailing dot appears to get stuck in a redirect loop and eventually raises `requests.exceptions.TooManyRedirects`. For example:

```python
import requests

res = requests.get("https://pyropus.ca./") 
```

I expected Requests to follow the redirect to the non-FQDN URL, `https://pyropus.ca/`, and return `200 OK`, like Chrome/Firefox or `curl` do. A workaround is to manually set the Host header without the trailing dot, which returns 200:

```python
custom_headers = {'Host': 'pyropus.ca'}
res = requests.get("https://pyropus.ca./", headers=custom_headers)
print(res.status_code)
```

System information: Requests version “Latest”, Python 3.10+, Linux. This was found while debugging a redirect loop in Fedora Infrastructure’s Anitya project. Is this a Requests bug in how trailing-dot FQDN redirects or the Host header are handled?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said Requests is unlikely to change this behavior. urllib3 intentionally strips the trailing dot for the HTTP/TLS stack while preserving it for DNS lookup, because TLS SNI/RFC 6066 and certificate validation generally require no trailing dot; the same domain had already been discussed in urllib3 issue #2873. The server is arguably misconfigured, and any change would need to happen in urllib3 because urllib3 controls Requests’ `Host` header handling; Requests would not carry a separate patch.

title: `http_proxy` bug with `starlette.responses.RedirectResponse`

qa_pairs.question:
In psf/requests, when I set the `http_proxy` environment variable and explicitly pass `proxies={'http': None, 'https': None}` to bypass the proxy, the first request avoids the proxy, but if it receives a redirect the redirected request picks up the environment proxy and fails. I expected both the original and redirected requests to bypass the proxy.

Reproduction:
```python
import os
import requests

# Set environment variable proxy (simulating a typical corporate environment)
os.environ['http_proxy'] = 'http://some.invalid.proxy:8080'

# Target URL that redirects to another domain
url = "http://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=http://example.com"

# Explicitly disable proxy
resp = requests.get(url, proxies={'http': None, 'https': None})
print(resp.status_code)
```

I suggested changing `sessions.py` line 316 from:
`new_proxies = resolve_proxies(prepared_request, proxies, self.trust_env)`
to:
`new_proxies = resolve_proxies(prepared_request, proxies, self.trust_env if proxies is None else False)`

Should redirected requests also honor the explicit `proxies={'http': None, 'https': None}` and avoid environment proxies, or is there another recommended way to fully disable proxy use across redirects?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said this is working as intended: disabling proxies for the initial request does not necessarily extend to redirects, because redirects move outside the explicitly declared intent and could otherwise leak information. To fully disable system-defined proxies, create a `Session` with `trust_env` disabled; alternatively disable auto-redirects with `allow_redirects=False` and handle each request manually, or use `no_proxy` for domains that should avoid proxy usage. The proposed change was rejected as incorrect semantics and potentially a security issue; Requests is defaulting to the secure behavior.

title: requests fails to connect even if trusted leaf certificate is provided when server's cert chain is incomplete

qa_pairs.answer: Use a custom `requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter` that passes a custom `ssl.SSLContext` to urllib3, set `context.verify_flags |= ssl.VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN`, and load the trusted leaf certificate with `context.load_verify_locations(...)`. The maintainers indicated they do not intend to change requests' default behavior right now; this should be accomplished with a custom adapter, which has historically been their suggestion for such use cases.

title: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED when using custom root CA in Windows

qa_pairs.answer: This appears to be the same problem already reported to CPython in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/135408. From: Juho Forsén via Fulldisclosure <fulldisclosure () seclists org>
```
Date: Sat, 31 May 2025 06:30:50 +0000
The PSF requests library (https://github.com/psf/requests & https://pypi.org/project/requests/) leaks .netrc
```

title: `SSLCertVerificationError` when fetching `https://od.moi.gov.tw/api/v1/`

qa_pairs.answer: The error is not specific to Requests or certifi; it comes from the Python standard library/OpenSSL verification layer. The issue appears to be that `VERIFY_X509_STRICT` and `VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN` are set, and in strict mode OpenSSL requires the optional Subject Key Identifier to be present; the `TWCA Global Root CA` used by related `*.tw` domains, and likely `od.moi.gov.tw`, does not have it. The maintainer/community therefore treated this as likely working as designed, with related discussion/reporting in CPython, urllib3, OpenSSL, and Arch Linux infrastructure issues.

title: Python 3.13: an unexpected `Authorization` header because of NETRC file

qa_pairs.answer: This comes from a Python netrc behavior change introduced in Python 3.11: for 3.11+, a netrc entry without username, account, or password is treated as valid. Requests previously got a `NetrcParseError` and skipped it, but now receives `('', '', '')`, which is truthy and gets turned into an Authorization header for `:` (`Basic Og==`). Requests considered its current behavior wrong, and PR #7205 was opened to skip netrc entries entirely when no auth info is found; once merged, it should be fixed in the next release.

title: Change auth.py to be used in a FIPS system

qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said the security concern should not be framed as MD5 being the security mechanism here: in HTTP Digest Authentication the hashing algorithm is a protocol detail, the server chooses the algorithm, and RFC 7616 notes algorithm agility does not make human-memorable passwords meaningfully more secure. The relevant security controls are a high-entropy password, TLS, and using Digest auth only with trusted servers. A PR was opened to address the issue: https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/7310, but it was left out of that day's release to allow time for comment.

title: Deprecated `HTTPAdapter.get_connection()` method is never called, causing breakage without deprecation warnings

qa_pairs.question:
After upgrading several of certbot's packages, including `requests` to 2.32.3, we started experiencing confusing DNS resolution errors with no clear cause. After bisecting, we isolated `requests` as the source and saw that 2.32.2 deprecated the `HTTPAdapter.get_connection()` method we used.

The change that deprecated `get_connection()` also causes it never to be called by `Session`, so the `DeprecationWarning` added in https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6710 is never printed. I would expect a minor version upgrade not to cause a breaking change.

Expected result: `HTTPAdapter.get_connection()` should still be called, resulting in no breaking changes and giving users the deprecation warning; or at least `Session` should check if `get_connection` is defined and print the deprecation warning then.

Actual result: `HTTPAdapter.get_connection()` is silently left uncalled, causing breakage.

Why did this breaking behavior happen, and what is the intended workaround for users overriding `HTTPAdapter.get_connection()`?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said the linked PR #6710 was only partway through the issue: it provided a public API for users overriding `get_connection`, while the initial breakage came from #6655, which addressed CVE-2024-35195. Requests generally avoids breaking changes in minor patch versions, but this change was made because users were unknowingly exposing data over unverified connections, and the impact was not fully assessed before 2.32.0. The workaround provided in #6710 is the backwards-compatible middle ground to keep adapters using a custom `get_connection` working with the least amount of work going forward.

title: SSLCertVerificationError - unable to get local issuer certificate

qa_pairs.question:
In psf/requests, version 2.32.0 introduced SSLContext changes from the release history: "verify=True now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (#6667)".

We are making HTTPS requests on Windows to webservers signed by a local root CA. The certificate chain is installed correctly on the Windows station, and requests 2.31.1 works as expected. With requests 2.32.x, we get:

`SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1125)')))`

This code works in 2.31.1 but not in 2.32.x:

```python
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
import requests
from requests.packages.urllib3.util.ssl_ import create_urllib3_context

class SSLContextAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
    def init_poolmanager(self, *args, **kwargs):
        context = create_urllib3_context()
        context.load_default_certs()  # this loads the system's CA certificates
        kwargs['ssl_context'] = context
        return super().init_poolmanager(*args, **kwargs)

SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.mount('https://', SSLContextAdapter())
SESSION.get(MY_URL_SIGNED_BY_LOCAL_ROOT_CA, headers = headers, verify  = True)
```

If we modify the code to call the private global `_preloaded_ssl_context`, it works, but that does not seem like the right approach:

```python
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter, _preloaded_ssl_context
import requests


class SSLContextAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
    def init_poolmanager(self, *args, **kwargs):
        _preloaded_ssl_context.load_default_certs() # this loads the system's CA certificates
        return super().init_poolmanager(*args, **kwargs)

SESSION = requests.Session()
SESSION.mount('https://', SSLContextAdapter())
SESSION.get(MY_URL_SIGNED_BY_LOCAL_ROOT_CA, headers = headers, verify  = True)
```

What is the recommended way to use `load_default_certs()` with a custom `HTTPAdapter` in requests 2.32.x, especially using the proposed changes in PR #6716 with a custom SSLContext adapter?
qa_pairs.answer:
Create and modify the custom SSL context in the adapter’s `__init__`, then override `build_connection_pool_key_attributes` and put that context into `pool_kwargs['ssl_context']`. The maintainer suggested using the same pattern as Requests’ `_preloaded_ssl_context` handling, optionally only applying it when `verify is True`.

Something like this:
```python
class SSLContextAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
    def __init__(
        self,
        pool_connections=DEFAULT_POOLSIZE,
        pool_maxsize=DEFAULT_POOLSIZE,
        max_retries=DEFAULT_RETRIES,
        pool_block=DEFAULT_POOLBLOCK,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.custom_context = create_urllib3_context()
        # Any cert modifications can be done here (if you need this per request,
        # do it in the build_connection_pool_key_attributes below.)
        self.custom_context.load_default_certs()
    
    [...]
    
    def build_connection_pool_key_attributes(self, request, verify, cert=None):
        host_params, pool_kwargs = super().build_connection_pool_key_attributes(request, verify, cert)
        pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] = self.custom_context  # you can put this behind a verify is True conditional too
        return host_params, pool_kwargs
```

Context: I’m building a scanner called QuantumMigrate that audits codebases for quantum-vulnerable crypto usage, and running it on this repository flagged 174 usages in `src/` alone, which is expected because the library implements RSA and ECC. I noticed `ssh.py` has RSA and ECC key types for SSH and that OpenSSH merged experimental support for ML-KEM-768 in OpenSSH 9.0; `_oid.py` lines 128-148 include SHA1 and MD5 in the OID signature algorithm map, which I understand is needed for parsing legacy certs but I wondered about deprecation warnings when used for signing; and `ec.py` / `rsa.py` contain the core implementations. Since OpenSSL 3.5 shipped post-quantum support in March 2026 and cryptography wraps OpenSSL, are there plans to add ML-KEM and ML-DSA alongside RSA/ECC, surface SSH ML-KEM support once stable, or track SLH-DSA? Is there an existing tracking issue I missed or a preferred way to contribute PQC primitives if OpenSSL exposes them?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer answered that the next release will include ML-KEM and ML-DSA support. They also stated that SLH-DSA is tracked separately in issue #14419.

title: Accessing unrelated extensions fails when BasicConstraints encodes default `ca:FALSE`

qa_pairs.question:
In pyca/cryptography 46.0.6 on Python 3.13.5, Debian Trixie amd64, accessing unrelated X.509 extensions fails when a certificate's BasicConstraints extension explicitly encodes the DER default `ca:FALSE`.

The certificate is a real certificate observed in a Certificate Transparency log. OpenSSL parses it without errors and shows `CA:FALSE` in Basic Constraints and a valid SAN (`DNS:receptum-apteekkiverkko.maxx.fi, IP Address:83.150.105.126`). The BasicConstraints extension contains `30 03 01 01 00`, a SEQUENCE with an explicit `BOOLEAN FALSE`; per RFC 5280/DER the `ca` field defaults to `FALSE` and should be omitted.

Minimal PoC:

```python
from cryptography import x509

der = open("entry_0046.der", "rb").read()
cert = x509.load_der_x509_certificate(der)

# This works fine:
print(cert.subject)
print(cert.issuer)

# This fails, even though SAN is valid:
san = cert.extensions.get_extension_for_class(x509.SubjectAlternativeName)
```

Output:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "poc.py", line 8, in <module>
    san = cert.extensions.get_extension_for_class(x509.SubjectAlternativeName)
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
  ...
ValueError: error parsing asn1 value: ParseError { kind: EncodedDefault, location: ["BasicConstraints::ca"] }
```

OpenSSL output for the same certificate includes:

```text
$ openssl x509 -inform DER -in entry_0046.der -text -noout
Certificate:
    Data:
        Version: 3 (0x2)
        Serial Number:
            01:99:3d:78:70:fe:f2:ca:f0:9b:b6:c9:d1:78:28
        Signature Algorithm: sha512WithRSAEncryption
        Issuer: C=FI, O=Digi- ja vaestotietovirasto CA, OU=Sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon palveluvarmenteet, CN=DVV Social Welfare and Healthcare Service Certificates - G3R
        Validity
            Not Before: Oct 22 21:00:00 2025 GMT
            Not After : Oct 22 20:59:59 2026 GMT
        Subject: C=FI, ST=FINLAND, L=Naantali, O=Naantalin 2. apteekki, serialNumber=1.2.246.553.1.853.13.0, CN=83.150.105.126
        X509v3 extensions:
            X509v3 Basic Constraints: critical
                CA:FALSE
            X509v3 Subject Alternative Name:
                DNS:receptum-apteekkiverkko.maxx.fi, IP Address:83.150.105.126
```

Since extension parsing appears to be all-or-nothing, this makes every extension inaccessible. Is this expected behavior in cryptography? Should accessing an unrelated extension like `SubjectAlternativeName` avoid failing due to a strict-DER violation in `BasicConstraints`, either by parsing extensions lazily or by accepting this common invalid DER encoding?
qa_pairs.answer:
This is an intentional design behavior.

In reverse order: We do not accept invalid DER, except in exceedingly rare cases. (See https://alexgaynor.net/2025/mar/25/postels-law-and-the-three-ring-circus/)

As for the issue of unrelated extensions, the most recent time this was brought up was https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/issues/13504#issuecomment-3368256526 (but I'm reasonably certain there's been other issues about this)

title: Extension criticality in EE certificates

qa_pairs.question:
In pyca/cryptography's x509 verification policy, how should CA/B Forum TLS BR criticality value `N` be interpreted for end-entity certificate extensions: as `Criticality::NonCritical` or `Criticality::Agnostic`? The current implementation in `extensions.rs` seems inconsistent: I hit an error when an Extended Key Usage extension was marked critical, even though RFC 5280 appears to allow critical EKU in some cases, while the BR table marks EKU as `N` / non-critical. At the same time, `subjectKeyIdentifier` is also `N` and `NOT RECOMMENDED` in the BRs, but the code marks it as `Criticality::Agnostic`.

CA/B Forum TLS BR 2.2.2 section 7.1.2.7.6 lists subscriber certificate extensions as:

| Extension | Presence | Critical | Description |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| authorityInformationAccess | MUST | N | See Section 7.1.2.7.7 |
| authorityKeyIdentifier | MUST | N | See Section 7.1.2.11.1 |
| certificatePolicies | MUST | N | See Section 7.1.2.7.9 |
| extKeyUsage | MUST | N | See Section 7.1.2.7.10 |
| subjectAltName | MUST | * | See Section 7.1.2.7.12 |
| nameConstraints | MUST NOT | ‐ |  - |
| keyUsage | SHOULD | Y |  See Section 7.1.2.7.11 |
| basicConstraints | MAY  | Y |  See Section 7.1.2.7.8 |
| crlDistributionPoints | * |  N |  See Section 7.1.2.11.2 |
| Signed Certificate Timestamp List | MAY  | N |  See Section 7.1.2.11.3 |
| subjectKeyIdentifier | NOT RECOMMENDED | N |  See Section 7.1.2.11.4 |
| Any other extension | NOT RECOMMENDED | ‐ |  See Section 7.1.2.11.5 |

CA/B Forum TLS BR 2.2.2 section 7.1.2 says:
```text
If the CA asserts compliance with these Baseline Requirements, all certificates that it issues MUST
comply with one of the following certificate profiles, which incorporate, and are derived from RFC
5280.
```

RFC 5280 says about EKU:
```text
   If a CA includes extended key usages to satisfy such applications,
   but does not wish to restrict usages of the key, the CA can include
   the special KeyPurposeId anyExtendedKeyUsage in addition to the
   particular key purposes required by the applications.  Conforming CAs
   SHOULD NOT mark this extension as critical if the anyExtendedKeyUsage
   KeyPurposeId is present.  Applications that require the presence of a
   particular purpose MAY reject certificates that include the
   anyExtendedKeyUsage OID but not the particular OID expected for the
   application.
```

The relevant code is:
```rust
            subject_key_identifier: ExtensionValidator::maybe_present(
                SUBJECT_KEY_IDENTIFIER_OID,
                Criticality::Agnostic,
                None,
            ),
[...]
            // CA/B: 7.1.2.7.10: Subscriber Certificate Extended Key Usage
            // NOTE: CABF requires EKUs in EE certs, while RFC 5280 does not.
            extended_key_usage: ExtensionValidator::maybe_present(
                EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE_OID,
                Criticality::NonCritical,
                Some(Arc::new(ee::extended_key_usage)),
            ),
```

Should `N` in the BR mean `Criticality::NonCritical` or `Criticality::Agnostic` for pyca/cryptography? More generally, should I change EKU to `Agnostic` to match the other extension criticality checks, or should the validator follow the BRs unless overridden? The current state appears to be: SKI is `Agnostic` when the BR says `N`, KU is `Agnostic` when the BR says `Y`, BC is `Agnostic` when the BR says `Y`, and EKU is `NonCritical` even though `Agnostic` might make sense from RFC 5280 usage-enforcement perspective.
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainers interpret the CA/B Forum criticality symbols as: `-` means not applicable, `*` means agnostic, and `Y`/`N` mean must be critical / must not be critical respectively. Their policy is to align with the BRs or RFC 5280 as appropriate, but to be laxer when required for interoperability in practice or when a property is not enforced by other validators; places where cryptography is laxer than the BRs are generally intentional. For EKU, they considered the current `NonCritical` behavior to match the BRs and did not identify an interop risk requiring a change.

title: On some plateforms, DHParameterNumbers performance is 100x slower

qa_pairs.question:
In pyca/cryptography, why is `DHParameterNumbers.parameters()` around 100x slower on OpenBSD/LibreSSL than on Debian/OpenSSL for RFC 3526 modp8192 parameters, and am I doing something wrong?

Reproducer:
```python
from cryptography.hazmat.backends import default_backend
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh import DHParameterNumbers

# modp8192 parameters
# https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3526 sect 7
g = 2
m = 

pn = DHParameterNumbers(m, g)
params = pn.parameters(default_backend())
```

Observed timings, both in Hyper-V VMs:

| OS | Flavor | Python | Time to run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debian 13 | OpenSSL 3.5.1 (FIPS: False, Legacy: True) | 3.13.5 | 0m0.086s real 0m0.069s user 0m0.017s system |
| OpenBSD 78 | LibreSSL 4.2.0 (FIPS: False, Legacy: False) | 3.12.11 | 1m03.48s real 1m03.32s user 0m00.08s system |
qa_pairs.answer: This was due to LibreSSL’s handling of DH checks for these parameters, not something the reporter was doing wrong in cryptography. LibreSSL landed code to skip the well-known parameters, with the main change in OpenBSD commit `9ac14cf7a1b28db2437e849540c0abe6a436a03d` and a follow-on adding RFC 7919 primes. The issue should no longer be a problem with LibreSSL 4.3.0 and later.

title: Add binding for SSL_get0_group_name to support PQC key exchange group detection

qa_pairs.question:
I maintain a Python tool that uses pyOpenSSL to initiate TLS handshakes and probe servers for their TLS support. I want to extend it to capture post-quantum cryptography readiness by detecting which key exchange group is actually negotiated during connections.

OpenSSL 3.5 added ML-KEM support and hybrid ECDH/PQ TLS groups such as `X25519MLKEM768`, `SecP256r1MLKEM768`, and `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`. OpenSSL documentation says `SSL_get0_group_name` is preferred for retrieving the negotiated group name:

> See also SSL_get0_group_name(3) which returns the name of the negotiated group directly and is generally preferred over SSL_get_negotiated_group().

`SSL_get0_group_name` was introduced in OpenSSL 3.2, while the hybrid PQC groups motivating this request require OpenSSL 3.5. The OpenSSL source for `SSL_get0_group_name` is at https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/53eb2363a1e6336a40a64b3f7b9f09eca95fabef/ssl/s3_lib.c#L5244, and it was introduced in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/68668243b176cd2bc53a83c6768d4f39930ba8ed.

I would like to contribute support in two places:

1. In `cryptography`, add bindings for `SSL_get0_group_name`, likely with appropriate OpenSSL 3.2+ version guards, following the patterns for similar functions. One place I looked at for version-guarding patterns is https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/blob/5cf5edf1b36afc8400e5b6d3975d0b15380f3eff/src/cryptography/hazmat/backends/openssl/backend.py#L288.
2. In `pyOpenSSL`, expose this as a new method such as `get_group_name()` on the SSL module's `Connection` class, similar conceptually to `get_cipher_list()`.

My local `nox -e local` succeeds, I have been reading `c-bindings.rst` and `ssl.py`, and I have joined `#pyca` IRC. I also noticed related discussion around setting curves in https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/issues/10797.

Given that OpenSSL 3.5.0 release notes say the default TLS group list now includes `?*X25519MLKEM768 / ?*X25519:?secp256r1 / ?X448:?secp384r1:?secp521r1 / ?ffdhe2048:?ffdhe3072`, I am unsure whether a client will negotiate `X25519MLKEM768` preferentially if the server supports it, or whether non-PQC groups would need to be excluded using something like `SSL_CTX_set1_groups_list`, which would require additional bindings.

Would adding an `SSL_get0_group_name` binding to `cryptography` and exposing it in pyOpenSSL be acceptable, and is there anything specific about the API or implementation approach I should account for?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said they would be okay with exposing `SSL_get0_group_name`. They noted that PQC-related APIs are diverging across OpenSSL and its forks, and that `SSL_get0_group_name` appears from the code to return the negotiated group name as defined by the TLS specs, though this is not officially documented. Before merging the cryptography binding, they wanted to see the pyOpenSSL PR first so the API and binding consumption could be agreed on; eventually the binding would also need to live in `rust-openssl` as cryptography migrates in that direction.

title: ML-KEM API Design

qa_pairs.question: For the proposed pyca/cryptography ML-KEM API, there is a strong desire not to expose expanded decapsulation keys as a serializable type, and to support only seed-based private key material. The proposed API is stateful: users load an `MLKEM768DecapKey` and then call `decap` on it with the ciphertext; there would not be any serialization in `decap`. Given SSH's use of ML-KEM, what are the SSH protocol requirements here? I am guessing SSH needs to obtain encapsulation keys as raw bytes with no SPKI wrapper, but what else is required, especially regarding expanded decapsulation/private keys?
qa_pairs.answer: An interoperability test between the pyca/cryptography ML-KEM support using BoringSSL and a prior liboqs-based implementation showed that everything SSH needed worked. `public_bytes_raw()` on the public key produced exactly the bytes needed on the SSH wire, and the ciphertext returned from `encap` was also in the required form; a 32-byte secret was exchanged successfully in both directions. SSH did not require serialization of private key data, so the API operating only on the seed rather than the expanded key was not a problem.

qa_pairs.question: In pyca/cryptography, I want to validate a certificate chain for a code-signing certificate using `x509.verification`. I understand there are client and server certificate verifiers, but I do not understand what the difference is and when to use each beyond the two named use cases of client or server certificate validation. How should I understand `ClientVerifier` versus `ServerVerifier`, especially for a case like code-signing where I may not know the subject in advance?
qa_pairs.answer: A `ServerVerifier` is built with a specific `subject`, and verification fails if the certificate does not contain a SAN extension matching the subject passed to `build_server_verifier`; it is intended for cases such as HTTPS where you know who the certificate must belong to. A `ClientVerifier` does not require the SAN extension to contain a specific value, so it can be used when you do not know the subject in advance; after `ClientVerifier.verify`, the SAN subjects are available via `VerifiedClient.subjects`. The default EE extension policies also differ: `ClientVerifier` requires the ClientAuth EKU and `ServerVerifier` requires the ServerAuth EKU, though a custom extension validator callback and custom extension policy can constrain EKU differently.
grounding_sources: cryptography x509.verification ClientVerifier, ServerVerifier, VerifiedClient, and ExtensionPolicy API behavior

qa_pairs.question: In pyca/cryptography's `x509.verification` APIs, I am confused why `PolicyBuilder` and `Policy` have different properties. `Policy` seems to have an EKU constraint that cannot be set by the builder, and there is a separate field for exactly that extension. qa_pairs.answer: The current `Policy` class is basically a direct mapping from a Rust struct containing context required for chain building and certificate verification/validation. Its main purpose is to expose that context to Python extension validation callbacks set by methods such as `ExtensionPolicy.may_be_present`, so callbacks can express constraints based on those parameters. Some properties, such as EKU, are not yet user-configurable, but can still be useful to callbacks; the maintainer acknowledged this may be confusing and leaks implementation details slightly, but preferred exposing extra properties rather than trying to predict every use case.

title: Thread-safety: data race in ImagingDefaultArena block cache (memory_get_block / memory_return_block)

qa_pairs.question:
In Pillow 10.4.0 on Linux x86_64 with Python 3.12, is `ImagingDefaultArena`'s block cache thread-safe when PIL image operations are offloaded concurrently via `asyncio.to_thread()` / `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and if not should Pillow add locking/per-thread arenas or document that multi-threaded usage requires `Image.core.set_blocks_max(0)`?

I observed that `ImagingDefaultArena` in `src/libImaging/Storage.c` uses shared mutable state (`blocks_cached`, `blocks_pool`) without synchronization. Multiple threads can call `memory_get_block` / `memory_return_block` concurrently when PIL's GIL-releasing C operations run in parallel:

```c
// memory_get_block (line 310) — no lock
if (arena->blocks_cached > 0) {
    arena->blocks_cached -= 1;                          // ← read-modify-write, no lock
    block = arena->blocks_pool[arena->blocks_cached];   // ← concurrent read, no lock
}

// memory_return_block (line 347) — no lock
if (arena->blocks_cached < arena->blocks_max) {
    arena->blocks_pool[arena->blocks_cached] = block;   // ← concurrent write, no lock
    arena->blocks_cached += 1;                          // ← read-modify-write, no lock
} else {
    free(block.ptr);
}
```

Race scenario:
```text
Thread A: reads blocks_cached = 19 (< blocks_max 20)
Thread B: reads blocks_cached = 19 (same stale value — no lock)
Thread A: writes blocks_pool[19] = block_A, increments to 20
Thread B: writes blocks_pool[19] = block_B (OVERWRITES block_A)

Result: block_A.ptr is permanently lost — malloc'd, never free'd.
```

Similarly, `memory_get_block` can hand the same cached block to two threads simultaneously, creating a use-after-free / double-free risk. The race window is narrow under the GIL but may occur during GIL-released operations like resize/encode, and could be more relevant with `asyncio.to_thread` and future free-threaded CPython. The workaround appears to be `Image.core.set_blocks_max(0)`.

Reproducer:

```python
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from PIL import Image

# This triggers concurrent access to ImagingDefaultArena from multiple threads.
# The race is probabilistic and more likely under sustained production load
# with longer GIL-released operations (resize, encode).
async def main():
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    loop.set_default_executor(ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=20))

    resolutions = [(512, 512), (1024, 1024), (1536, 1536), (2048, 2048)]

    async def process(res):
        def _work():
            img = Image.new("RGB", res)
            img.load()
        await asyncio.to_thread(_work)

    for _ in range(1000):
        await asyncio.gather(*[process(resolutions[i % 4]) for i in range(20)])

asyncio.run(main())
```

Suggested fixes are: add a `pthread_mutex` around `blocks_cached` / `blocks_pool` access in `memory_get_block` and `memory_return_block`, use per-thread arenas, or document that the block cache is not thread-safe and recommend `set_blocks_max(0)` for multi-threaded usage.
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer asked why Pillow 10.4.0 was being used instead of the latest version, noting that PR #8238 helped threading in `Storage.c` in Pillow 11.0.0 and asking whether the reporter could test a more recent version. They also stated that any fix would only be applied to new Pillow releases and quoted the release notes policy that functionality and security fixes should not be expected to be backported to earlier versions.

```python
    print("exit")
```

It can crash, or sometimes it does not crash. Sometimes I even see `exit` in the output and then the crash occurs. I tried adding print statements inside Pillow, but the crash seems random and I cannot pinpoint the exact spot.

Some commits I found:

- `1ee3bd1d9e1a96da01ba55aff376e214082bcba8` — crash already occurs
- `08d9c89d8a7db84e8145814bca36d7dd5b7465ce` — repo at this commit is good

qa_pairs.answer: A git bisect identified `84e275d90629bfdf508f81a1142eddd5d5ea46e4` as the first bad commit. That commit came from PR https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/pull/8390 and changed `src/PIL/ImageFile.py` with the message “Loading does not change mode.”

qa_pairs.question:
After investigating the random crash in Pillow dev with `pillow_heif`, I found that `zPug_3.heic` contains three images/frames with different modes:

```text
<pillow_heif.as_plugin.HeifImageFile image mode=RGB size=64x64>
<pillow_heif.as_plugin.HeifImageFile image mode=L size=64x64>
<pillow_heif.as_plugin.HeifImageFile image mode=RGB size=96x64>
```

It turns out that when the second frame has a different mode, after commit `84e275d90629bfdf508f81a1142eddd5d5ea46e4`, a new `Image.core.new` is not created, the mode does not change, and `pillow_heif` calculates the wrong stride based on the wrong mode (`RGB` vs `L`). Can Pillow revert commit `84e275d90629bfdf508f81a1142eddd5d5ea46e4`?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer response was that reverting is acceptable, but a good test case may be the hardest part. Further discussion suggested either reverting and deprecating or changing plugins so the core image is reset when mode or size changes; PR #8450 was created to try setting `self._im` to `None` at the end of `seek()` when the mode or size changes. If that suggestion is not preferred, the maintainer said they were happy to just revert the `load_prepare()` change.

title: ValueError: Decompressed Data Too Large

qa_pairs.question:
I'm using Pillow 9.5.0 on Ubuntu 22.04 with Python 3.10.12. I attempted to open a PNG that was created with Pillow, expecting it to open successfully, but Pillow throws `ValueError: Decompressed Data Too Large`. Other details from `PIL.features.pilinfo()` include ZLIB support loaded 1.2.11 and PNG open/save support. The reproducer is:

```python
img = Image.open('001041.png')
```

The image is `001041.png` from the issue attachment. Why is Pillow refusing to open this PNG, and how can I open it?
qa_pairs.answer:
You are hitting Pillow's PNG decompressed text chunk limit. `PIL.PngImagePlugin.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK` defaults to 1048576 bytes to limit decompressed iTXt or zTXt chunks and prevent decompression bombs. You can increase it before opening the file:

```python
from PIL import Image, PngImagePlugin
PngImagePlugin.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK = 2 * 1024 * 1024
Image.open('001041.png')
```

qa_pairs.question: The workaround of increasing `PngImagePlugin.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK` lets me open the PNG, but I still think this is a bug or at least a bad default/error message. The PNG was generated by Pillow, so I expected Pillow to be able to open it, and OpenCV, GIMP, qiv, etc. can open it without adjusting internal constants. The image was generated using code that uses blenderproc to render 3D objects on top of OpenImages V7 background images. Is there anything Pillow should change, such as increasing the default maximum decompressed size or changing the error message to suggest increasing the limit?
qa_pairs.answer: The problematic part of the image is an ICC profile just over 1 MB; Pillow raises the error to prevent decompression bombs where compressed data expands excessively. Without a self-contained example, the maintainer concluded there was not anything else for Pillow to do about where the ICC profile came from, and raising an error on save would not be helpful. They created PR #8391 to change the error message to `Decompressed data too large for PngImagePlugin.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK`, so users can find the documentation explaining that individual compressed PNG chunks are limited by `PngImagePlugin.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK`, default 1 MB.

title: Is Pillow affected by WebP vulnerability?

qa_pairs.question:
Is Pillow affected by CVE-2023-4863 in libwebp when using Pillow versions < 10.0.1? I know CVE-2023-4863 was fixed in Pillow 10.0.1, but I cannot update to that version at the moment. I want to understand whether Pillow actually uses the vulnerable functionality, or whether the CVE can be whitelisted because use of the vulnerable library is excluded by Pillow's functional design.

Environment:
* OS: 
* Python: 
* Pillow: < 10.0.1
qa_pairs.answer:
Pillow calls WebPAnimDecoderGetNext, which calls WebPDecode, calling DecodeInto, calling VP8LDecodeHeader, calling DecodeImageStream, calling ReadHuffmanCodes, calling ReadHuffmanCode, calling VP8LBuildHuffmanTable, calling BuildHuffmanTable - so I don't see why we wouldn't be vulnerable.

You might also be interested in this distinction - the source code of Pillow itself did not really change in 10.0.1 to address this situation. 10.0.1 was released to provide new wheels to those who do not compile Pillow from source. You could use an earlier version of Pillow with a recent version of libwebp and not be vulnerable.
grounding_sources: Pillow WebP decoding call path: WebPAnimDecoderGetNext -> WebPDecode -> DecodeInto -> VP8LDecodeHeader -> DecodeImageStream -> ReadHuffmanCodes -> ReadHuffmanCode -> VP8LBuildHuffmanTable -> BuildHuffmanTable

title: May I ask if Pillow 9.3.0 (windows) involves the CVE-2023-45853 vulnerability in zlib?

qa_pairs.question: On Windows 10, I am using Pillow 9.3.0 with zlib 1.2.13. NVD lists CVE-2023-45853 for zlib/minizip at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-45853. Does Pillow 9.3.0 for Windows involve the vulnerable minizip-related modules, or is it affected by this zlib CVE?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said no: MiniZip is not a supported part of the zlib product, and Pillow’s Windows build merely builds `zlib.lib` via `win32\Makefile.msc` rather than taking the separate steps needed to involve minizip. They also pointed to a zlib comment saying “This is not a zlib vulnerability.” Separately, they recommended upgrading from Pillow 9.3.0 because Pillow has fixed various security problems since then.

title: PPM "Channel value too large" error

qa_pairs.question:
We are using Pillow 9.4.0 on Windows 10 with Python 3.9 to read PPM images of 1280x1024 or 1920x1080 pixels in RGB 24 bits with a maxval of 255 in the header, then convert them to PNG. Opening/showing one such PPM fails with `Channel value too large for this mode`; in one case Pillow reported the value `20458` even though no channel data is higher than 255. Investigation suggested that `_read_block` concatenates a trailing token from the previous block with the next block without a separator:
```python
if half_token:
    block = half_token + block  # stitch half_token to new block
```
so `... 204 ]` plus `[58 ...` becomes `[20458 ...` instead of `[204 58 ...`. I locally tried changing it to:
```python
if half_token:
    block = half_token + b' ' + block  # stitch half_token to new block
    half_token = False
```
A reproducible test was:
```python
# Python39
from PIL import Image
im = Image.open("mignon1280.ppm")
im.show()
```
Since we can’t really wait a month, is there a local/temporary fix or workaround we can use for converting these PPM images to PNG?
qa_pairs.answer:
A temporary workaround is to override `PpmPlainDecoder._read_block` so it reads the entire file data at once:
```python
from PIL.PpmImagePlugin import PpmPlainDecoder
PpmPlainDecoder._read_block = lambda self: self.fd.read()

from PIL import Image
im = Image.open("mignon1280.ppm")
im.show()
```
The maintainer also created PR #7052 to resolve the issue, expected to be included in Pillow 9.5.0, and noted that the bug was also a security issue because the lingering half token could consume unexpected resources.

title: `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is silenced in nested transactions - including ApplicationRecord callbacks

qa_pairs.question:
In Rails latest from main on Ruby 3.4.4, `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside a nested transaction appears to be swallowed, so the outer transaction still commits. Reproduction:

```ruby
    user = User.create!(name: "john")

    assert_equal true, user.active
    assert_equal true, user.email.active

    User.transaction do
      user.active = false

      Email.transaction do
        email = user.email
        email.active = false
        email.save

        raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
      end
    end

    user.reload

    # Both are committed to the database even though an ActiveRecord::Rollback was raised
    assert_equal true, user.active, "Expect that the whole transaction fails and the user is not saved"
    assert_equal true, user.email.active, "Expect that the email is not updated"
```

The same happens from an `ApplicationRecord` callback:

```ruby
# definition
class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  after_create :create_email_for_user

  private

  def create_email_for_user
    email = build_email(email_address: "#{name}@example.com")

    unless email.save
      errors.add(:base, email.errors.full_messages.first || "Email creation failed")
      raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
    end
  end
end

# usage
user = User.new(name: "john")
saved = User.transaction do
  # This will attempt to create an email with `john@example.com` which already exists
  # and raise an ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid error in `create_email_for_user`
  user.save
end

user.reload

# user is successfully saved, this fails:
refute user.persisted?, "User should not be persisted since create_email_for_user raised an ActiveRecord::Rollback error"
```

Is this a Rails bug? Should the `ActiveRecord::Rollback` bubble up instead of being silenced in nested transactions, or should Rails otherwise prevent/document manual raising of `ActiveRecord::Rollback`?
qa_pairs.answer:
This is expected behavior and well documented, not a bug:
https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/ConnectionAdapters/DatabaseStatements.html#method-i-transaction

Nested transactions in Rails are joinable by default. That means the inner transaction does not start a new database transaction, so raising `ActiveRecord::Rollback` there does not issue a SQL `ROLLBACK`. The exception is intentionally swallowed, and the outer transaction can still commit.

At the SQL level, most databases don’t support true nested `BEGIN/COMMIT`. There is only one transaction per connection. To roll back part of a transaction, SQL uses SAVEPOINTS, not nested `BEGIN`s:
```
BEGIN;
  INSERT INTO posts ...;          -- first
  SAVEPOINT sp1;
    INSERT INTO posts ...;        -- second
    ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp1;    -- undo only inner work
COMMIT;
```
Rails maps this explicitly via ^requires_new: true`:
```
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  Post.create!(title: "first")
  ActiveRecord::Base.transaction(requires_new: true) do
    Post.create!(title: "second")
    raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
  end
end
```

Without `requires_new`, there is no SQL boundary to roll back so the behavior is correct by design.

Changing this would be a significant backward-compatibility change, so it’s likely outside the scope of a bugfix. As already discovered, this is being discussed in more depth in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44518, which seems like the appropriate place for exploring a broader proposal or deprecation path.

title: Deadlocked transactions are still seen as "usable" for MySQL (trilogy / mysql2)

qa_pairs.question:
In Rails 8.1.1 on Ruby 3.4.4, using MySQL via trilogy/mysql2, a deadlocked transaction can still appear usable. Reproduction gist: https://gist.github.com/ipvalverde/2d2f6b91d593e09b89a86a7c61a3ca5b. Important bit:

```ruby
Account.transaction do
  Account.create!(name: "Account in top-level transaction", balance: 50)

  begin
    puts "1) Is transaction open? #{Account.connection.transaction_open?}"

    # consider the logic in here will raise a deadlock:
    Account.lock.find(1).update!(balance: 10)
    Account.lock.find(2).update!(balance: 20)

  rescue ActiveRecord::Deadlocked => e
    puts "2) Is transaction open? #{Account.connection.transaction_open?}"

    # Everything up to this point is DISCARDED from the Database perspective.
    # No account being created, no accounts being updated.
    
  end

  # This will write directly to the database - no valid transactions in here.
  Account.create!(name: "Last account in top-level transaction", balance: 999)

  # this will be a no-op since there's no transaction open
  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
end
```

Expected behavior: any database writes, and maybe reads, in code intended to run within a transaction should fail if there is no transaction open. PostgreSQL behaves as expected because after the deadlock, trying to create an account raises:

```text
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: PG::InFailedSqlTransaction: ERROR:  current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block
```

Actual behavior: after the transaction deadlocks and is killed, if `ActiveRecord::Deadlocked` is swallowed, later code inside the transaction block writes directly to the database, while the transaction still appears open/usable. Why is the deadlocked MySQL transaction still seen as a healthy transaction, and what should be fixed?
qa_pairs.answer: The transaction state handling appears to be the cause. PR #44127 changed transaction state behavior so an `invalidated` transaction that is rolled back transitions from `invalidated` to `rolledback`, making it look like a healthy transaction even though it is not. The proposed fix is to preserve the `invalidated` state without fully invalidating the connection.

title: Migrations that alter SQLite table structure can cause data loss

qa_pairs.question:
In Rails' SQLite adapter, migrations that alter table structure (for example, a mere `add_foreign_key`) can wipe out a production SQLite table, as described in https://kyrylo.org/software/2025/09/27/a-mere-add-foreign-key-can-wipe-out-your-whole-rails-sqlite-production-table.html. Rails appears to already disable and re-enable the `foreign_keys` PRAGMA around table changes since https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/45881b0a64b4039e3b0d27e2c4d959dc2d744b9d, but the current ordering seems to be:

```
transaction do
  disable_referential_integrity do
```

I think it should instead be:

```
disable_pragma_foreign_keys do
  transaction do
    enable_defer_foreign_keys do
```

because SQLite documents that `PRAGMA foreign_keys` “is a no-op within a transaction; foreign key constraint enforcement may only be enabled or disabled when there is no pending BEGIN or SAVEPOINT,” while `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys` is set per transaction and therefore has to be inside the transaction block. Should Rails change the SQLite table-recreation flow to disable `PRAGMA foreign_keys` outside the transaction, perform the change transactionally, and use deferred foreign keys inside the transaction?
qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said the fix is ready for review. It disables foreign key enforcement before the table recreation process and re-enables it afterwards, with the sequence: disable foreign keys outside the transaction, perform table recreation inside a transaction, re-enable foreign keys, and validate schema integrity with `PRAGMA foreign_key_check`.

title: ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector sets cookies on asset requests

In a Rails app using automatic DB switching (docs: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_multiple_databases.html#activating-automatic-role-switching) with the default resolver `ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver` and context `ActiveRecord::Middleware::DatabaseSelector::Resolver::Session`, asset requests appear to get a `Set-Cookie` header in the response. Actual behavior: asset requests have a `set-cookie` header in the response.

title: Handle links and other safe content inside translations

qa_pairs.question: In Rails translations, I want to interpolate safe HTML such as a `link_to` result without forcing the translation key itself to know whether the interpolation contains HTML. Currently I have to do either: ```erb <%= t(".text", insert: link_to(t(".insert"), root_path)).html_safe %> ``` or: ```erb <%= t(".text_html", insert: link_to(t(".insert"), root_path)) %> ``` But the `text_html` translation should not have to know whether `insert` contains HTML, and the Rails i18n guide does not explain a nice way to do this. Ideally Rails i18n would be aware of `SafeBuffer` and safely join content like this: ```yml text: some <> text with an %{insert} text_html: some <> text with an %{insert} insert: a link, properly escaping <> ``` ```erb <%= t(".text", insert: link_to(t(".insert"), root_path)) %> ``` Since `link_to` returns an `html_safe` string, the desired output would be: ```html some <> text with an a link, properly escaping <> ``` Is there a secure/simple way for Rails or rails-i18n to handle links and other safe content inside translations automatically using `SafeBuffer`, rather than requiring manual `html_safe` or `_html` keys for this case?
qa_pairs.answer: A community member said they had implemented a version of this behavior and shared it as a gist: https://gist.github.com/henrik/f6619f298de3b6f59dfba589fa5476d7. They said they would like something like that to become part of Rails or rails-i18n.

title: ActiveRecord call `.lease_connection` inside `.transaction` cause connection leak

qa_pairs.question:
In Rails ActiveRecord, calling `lease_connection` inside a transaction appears to leave a connection leased to the current thread after the transaction. Reproduction in `rails c`:
```ruby
puts "Before: #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.active_connection?}"
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  ActiveRecord::Base.lease_connection
end
puts "After: #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.active_connection?}"
```
Expected:
```ruby
Before:
After: 
```
Actual:
```ruby
Before:
After: #<ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::Mysql2Adapter>
```
This matters because our application mixes DB queries with slower HTTP requests and can hit MySQL connection limits; we need to return obtained DB connections to the pool before HTTP requests. We also saw it after adding `after_commit_everywhere` 1.6.0 to a Rails 7.2.2.1 app for `Sidekiq.transactional_push!`, where this leaks:
```ruby
class MyWorker
  include Sidekiq::Worker
  sidekiq_options queue: :default

  def perform; end
end

puts "Before: #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.active_connection?}"
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  MyWorker.perform_async
end
puts "After: #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.active_connection?}"
```
The trace goes through:
https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq/blob/v6.5.12/lib/sidekiq/transaction_aware_client.rb#L16
https://github.com/Envek/after_commit_everywhere/blob/v1.6.0/lib/after_commit_everywhere.rb#L100
https://github.com/Envek/after_commit_everywhere/blob/v1.6.0/lib/after_commit_everywhere.rb#L111
https://github.com/Envek/after_commit_everywhere/blob/v1.6.0/lib/after_commit_everywhere.rb#L144
https://github.com/Envek/after_commit_everywhere/blob/v1.6.0/lib/after_commit_everywhere.rb#L172

System configuration: Rails 7.2.2.1 with Ruby 3.3.2, and Rails 8.0.2 with Ruby 3.4.4.

If `lease_connection` is designed to keep the connection leased until `release_connection`, how can I easily receive a connection without this sticky behavior in complicated nested code, e.g.:
```ruby
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  do_call
end

def do_call
  # ActiveRecord::Base.connection or something else that will release connection after #transaction block
end
```
qa_pairs.answer:
Call `release_connection` when you are done with a leased connection, or only check out connections where needed using `with_connection`; nested `with_connection` gives you the same connection. The sticky behavior was by design to avoid breaking code expecting sticky connections, per PR #51192. You can also wrap the whole thing in `.with_connection(prevent_permanent_checkout: true)`.

```ruby
# call `release_connection` when you're done with a connection
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  do_call
end
ActiveRecord::Base.release_connection

# or only checkout connections where you need them (nesting with_connection always gives you the same connection)
def do_call
  Base.with_connection do |c|
  end
end
```

```ruby
    t.datetime :updated_at
    t.integer :post_id
  end

  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.bigint :initial_comment_id
  end

  create_table :comments, force: true do |t|
    t.integer :post_id
  end

   add_foreign_key :posts, :comments, column: :initial_comment_id
    add_foreign_key :comments, :posts
    add_foreign_key :users, :posts
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :initial_comment, class_name: 'Comment', autosave: false, inverse_of: :post_as_initial_comment
  has_many :comments
  has_many :users, inverse_of: :post

  end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_one_attached :profile
  belongs_to :post
  after_save :override_blob_key

  def override_blob_key 
    profile.blob.key = "#{id}_#{(Time.now.to_f * 1000).to_i}"
  end
end

class Comment < ActiveRecord::Base
    belongs_to :post
    has_one :post_as_initial_comment, class_name: 'Post', foreign_key: 'initial_comment_id', inverse_of: :initial_comment
end

class BugTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def test_upload_and_download
    user = User.build(
      profile: {
        content_type: "text/plain",
        filename: "dummy.txt",
        io: ::StringIO.new("dummy"),
      }
    )

    comment = Comment.build
    post = Post.build(initial_comment: comment, comments: [comment], users: [user])
    post.save!

    assert_equal "dummy", user.profile.download
  end
end
```

Expected behavior: the file should have been uploaded.

Actual behavior: the file is not uploaded even though the attachments and blobs are saved. In `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model::class_methods#has_one_attached`, `attachment_changes` is `{}`, so `ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateOne#upload` was never reached. Is this a Rails/Active Storage bug related to these associations or the upload flow?

title: Upgrade transitive dependency qs to >= 6.14.1 to address CVE-2025-15284

qa_pairs.question: In stripe/stripe-node, the Stripe Node SDK currently pulls in `qs` as a transitive dependency via `stripe → qs@^6.11.0`, and that range resolves to a `qs` version vulnerable to CVE-2025-15284 / GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p. The vulnerability affects `qs` versions `< 6.14.1`, where the `arrayLimit` option can be bypassed using bracket notation such as `a[]=x`, allowing unbounded array creation and potentially causing Denial of Service via memory exhaustion. Even when applications configure `arrayLimit` in `qs.parse()`, the limit is ignored for bracket notation (`a[]=value`), so an attacker could submit a single crafted request that consumes excessive memory, especially in applications parsing user-controlled query strings or request bodies. Can the Stripe Node SDK upgrade its `qs` dependency to the patched version `qs >= 6.14.1`, which enforces `arrayLimit` consistently for both indexed and bracket notation? Reference: https://github.com/ljharb/qs/security/advisories/GHSA-6rw7-vpxm-498p
qa_pairs.answer: The Stripe team updated the version of `qs` and shipped version 20.1.1 of the Stripe Node SDK.

title: Upgrade `qs`

qa_pairs.answer: The maintainer said they updated the version of `qs` and shipped version 20.1.1 of the SDK. They thanked the reporter for reporting it.

title: cannot create bank object  with bank details

In stripe-node on Linux with Node 16.15, latest library version, and Stripe API version 2020-08-27, I am trying to create a customer bank account object using `customers.createSource` by passing bank account details as key/value pairs instead of passing a source ID, but I get a TypeScript typing issue and the documentation is vague about whether bank details can be passed directly. Should this work, and what should I do about the typing issue?

Code:
```JavaScript

  "cus_...",
  { source: {
    object: "bank_account",
    account_number: "110000000",
    routing_number: "000123456789",
    country: "US",
```

qa_pairs.answer: Stripe recommends using the PaymentMethod API instead, specifically the ACH Debit integration docs, and collecting bank account details client-side because passing raw bank account details server-side is dangerous and increases security/compliance burden.
